question:
**Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.**

The dog will whine at the door when he __**wants to go**__ out.
solution:
The correct answer is **3) No improvement**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The underlined part of the sentence, **"wants to go,"** is already grammatically correct.
 
• The verb** "wants" **is the correct form to use with the subject **"he,"** indicating the singular third person.
 
• The infinitive form "to go" follows the verb "wants" to express the desired action.
 
 
• *"The dog will whine at the door when he **wants to go**__ out."*
 
 
 
• This sentence accurately conveys that the dog expresses its desire to go outside by whining at the door.
 
• Let's analyze the other options:
 
• **wants to gone: **This option is grammatically incorrect. The correct form should be "wants to go" instead of "wants to gone." The infinitive form "to go" is used after "wants" to express the desired action.
 
• **want to go:** This option is grammatically incorrect. The verb form "want" does not match with the subject "he," which requires the singular form "wants."
 
• **wants to going:** This option is grammatically incorrect. The verb form "going" is not appropriate after "to" in this context. The correct form is "wants to go" to express the desired action.
 
• In conclusion, the original underlined part of the sentence is already correct, and no improvement is necessary.
